protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: PASS: At v2.2.4.2, unauthenticated TCP/7624 input reaches MsgQueue::readFromFd(), which reads up to 49152 bytes and passes them with char err[1024] to parseXMLChunk(). oneXMLchar() grows opening and closing tag strings without a length cap, then uses sprintf() to place both attacker-sized names in err when tags mismatch, permitting a stack-buffer overflow and daemon crash.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: PASS: An all-ref reverse -S search for the exact mismatch format string identifies 4d63b7497c1748e19be6fda6b262802fd7f0b043 as its first public write. The next commit, 290e14216103d2e6bee1594be08d9eb9f37fe68c, wires readXMLEle() to the TCP client path but does not first write the vulnerable formatting sink; later renames, reindents, moves, and the 2025 MsgQueue split are carriers, not BICs.
